mcqs.question: A 2 kg block rests on a horizontal rough surface. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface is 0.30. What is the maximum possible frictional force that can act on the block?
mcqs.explanation: The normal reaction N = mg = 2 kg × 10 m/s² = 20 N. Maximum static friction f_max = μ_s N = 0.30 × 20 N = 6 N. Hence option B is correct. The other values do not follow the f = μN relation.

mcqs.question: A 5 kg crate rests on a horizontal floor. The coefficients of static and kinetic friction are μ_s = 0.40 and μ_k = 0.30 respectively. A horizontal force of 15 N is applied. Which statement best describes the frictional forces before and after the crate starts moving?

options.A: Static friction is 8 N before motion and kinetic friction is 6 N after motion.
options.B: Static friction equals the applied 15 N before motion, and kinetic friction equals 15 N after motion.
options.C: Static friction equals the applied 15 N before motion, and kinetic friction is 15 N after motion because μ_k N = 15 N.
options.D: There is no friction before motion and kinetic friction of 15 N after motion.

mcqs.answer: Static friction equals the applied 15 N before motion, and kinetic friction equals 15 N after motion.
mcqs.explanation: Before motion, static friction adjusts to match the applied force up to its maximum value (μ_s N = 0.40×5×10 = 20 N). Since 15 N < 20 N, static friction equals the applied 15 N. Once the crate moves, kinetic friction is μ_k N = 0.30×5×10 = 15 N, which also equals the applied force for constant speed. Hence option B correctly captures the behaviour. Options A, C and D give incorrect values or misunderstand the role of static friction.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about limiting friction is correct?

options.A: Limiting friction is the maximum value of static friction just before motion starts.
options.B: Limiting friction is equal to kinetic friction for any pair of surfaces.
options.C: Limiting friction acts only when objects are already moving.
options.D: Limiting friction is independent of the nature of the contacting surfaces.

mcqs.answer: Limiting friction is the maximum value of static friction just before motion starts.
mcqs.explanation: Limiting (or maximum static) friction is the greatest static frictional force that can be exerted before relative motion begins; it is given by f_max = μ_s N. It is not equal to kinetic friction (option B), does not act after motion starts (option C), and depends on surface nature (option D). Hence A is correct.

mcqs.question: A 10 kg block slides down a rough inclined plane that makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.20. What is the magnitude of the kinetic frictional force acting on the block?
mcqs.explanation: Normal reaction N = mg cosθ = 10 kg × 10 m/s² × cos30° = 100 N × 0.866 ≈ 86.6 N. Kinetic friction f_k = μ_k N = 0.20 × 86.6 N ≈ 17.3 N. Therefore option B is correct. The other options result from incorrect normal force or omission of the cosine factor.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the coefficients of friction for a given pair of surfaces?

options.A: The coefficient of static friction is always less than the coefficient of kinetic friction.
options.B: The coefficient of static friction is always greater than or equal to the coefficient of kinetic friction.
options.D: The coefficients cannot be compared without knowing the normal force.

mcqs.answer: The coefficient of static friction is always greater than or equal to the coefficient of kinetic friction.
mcqs.explanation: For any pair of surfaces, μ_s ≥ μ_k because it is harder to start motion than to maintain it. Hence option B is correct. Option A reverses the relationship, C is false except for special cases, and D is irrelevant because coefficients are independent of normal force.

mcqs.question: A 2 kg block is placed on a rough inclined plane. The plane is gradually inclined until the block is just about to start sliding down when the angle reaches 30°. If the coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane is μ_s, what is the value of μ_s?
mcqs.explanation: At the point of impending motion, tanθ = μ_s. With θ = 30°, tan30° = 0.577. Therefore μ_s ≈ 0.577, which corresponds to option C. The other options do not satisfy the condition tanθ = μ_s for θ = 30°.

mcqs.question: Frictional force is best described as:

options.A: A force that acts only when objects are moving relative to each other.
options.B: A force that always acts parallel to the surface and opposes relative motion or the tendency of motion.
options.C: A force that acts perpendicular to the surface.
options.D: A force that depends only on the speed of the moving object.

mcqs.answer: A force that always acts parallel to the surface and opposes relative motion or the tendency of motion.
mcqs.explanation: Friction always acts parallel to the contacting surfaces and opposes relative motion or the tendency for motion. Option A ignores static friction, C describes the normal reaction, and D is incorrect because friction depends on the nature of surfaces and normal force, not solely on speed. Hence B is correct.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes static friction from kinetic friction?

options.A: Static friction acts when there is relative motion; kinetic friction acts when there is no motion.
options.B: Static friction has a constant value; kinetic friction varies up to a maximum.
options.C: Static friction prevents the start of motion up to a maximum value; kinetic friction opposes motion once it has started and generally has a lower constant value.
options.D: Both static and kinetic friction are independent of the nature of the surfaces.

mcqs.answer: Static friction prevents the start of motion up to a maximum value; kinetic friction opposes motion once it has started and generally has a lower constant value.
mcqs.explanation: Static friction adjusts up to its limiting value to prevent motion; kinetic friction acts once motion has begun and is usually lower and approximately constant (μ_k N). Option A reverses the definitions, B misstates the variability, and D ignores surface dependence. Therefore C is correct.
